problem_type: Configuration presence is conflated with certified credential execution readiness
symptom: A custom API key is saved, but Add Models disappears and its key editor treats the saved encrypted material as missing.
direct_cause: Renderer key writes correctly remain disabled until certification; hasApiKey is false for disabled material and configuration UI incorrectly uses that execution projection as storage presence.
class_root: Public connection metadata lacks a distinct non-authoritative stored-credential presence signal for configuration-only consumers.
internal_only_reason: The saved/unpublished lifecycle and public DTO semantics are application-owned; the failed native walk and rendererCatalogMutation/secrets code establish the cause without an external protocol assumption.
invariants: Stored credential presence never grants publication, health, spend or execution permission.
Configuration navigation can use retained encrypted material for existing explicit model-list and certification flows.
Missing or cleared material cannot be forged by a renderer vendor payload.
No credential value or ciphertext is exposed in the vendor DTO.

door_reduction.why_not: Generated reads cover existing connection UI, credential health, two public type contracts, exhaustive field classification and both locale compositions. Health and publication consumers intentionally retain the old ready signal; only stored-key presentation and configuration navigation use the new public presence boolean. No execution or persistence door is added.

generality_proof: Derive presence centrally from the encrypted record at public DTO projection, not from provider name or a UI-supplied field. Separate its configuration consumers from existing readiness consumers across saved, disabled, locked and cleared records.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Project stored encrypted-material presence without changing internal credential authority.
Permit only configuration navigation for saved material while preserving native-provider exclusions.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Saved-key presentation uses the presence signal; its independent health probe still uses hasApiKey.
Both home and detail Add Models commands share this existing gate.
Health probing retains execution-readiness hasApiKey and cannot be enabled by mere stored material.

recurrence.reason: Every custom relay key replacement enters the same deliberately disabled-until-certified state.
same_class_scan: Read rendererCatalogMutation, credentialRecordCounts, existingConnection decryption, CustomVendorManage and both Add Models entry points

prevention.invariant: Configuration-only stored presence is derived separately from executable readiness.
prevention.failure_mode: No usable key, publication or generation is granted by the presence bit; missing/decryption failures remain rejected by existing main-process resolution.
prevention.strategy: Add a derived public boolean and explicitly route only configuration consumers to it, retaining all readiness guards.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove readiness-as-storage checks only in configuration consumers; keep credential execution and publication unchanged.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party behavior determines the missing application-state distinction; safeStorage remains unchanged.

migration: No catalog schema migration: presence is derived on public reads and never trusted from persisted or renderer-authored fields. Existing encrypted records work unchanged.
residual_risks: Native zh/en post-edit configuration acceptance must pass before delivery.
Retained locked material is not usable until the system can decrypt it or the user replaces it.
Advertised model inventory is not proof every model can generate media.
